mainTopic: The מקדש שופר and trumpets, gold versus silver plating, the יובל and ראש השנה ברכות, and the start of the משנה on a cracked שופר
overview: The גמרא explains several details from the משנה about the שופר used in the בית המקדש. First, it shows that the gold on the ראש השנה שופר was near the mouthpiece but not where the lips touch, since gold there makes a שופר פסול. Next it asks how the שופר could be heard over the two trumpets blown with it. It first suggests that the long שופר blast was heard alone at the end, but drops this after a challenge from a שופר blown into a pit. Its final answer is that two sounds from two different people can be heard, especially a sound people love, like שופר, הלל or מגילה. The long blast is only a sign that the שופר is the main מצוה of the day. The fast-day שופר is silver, either because gathering instruments are silver or to save money, while ראש השנה gets gold to honor the יום טוב. רבא, a ברייתא and a פסוק teach that blowing שופר and trumpets together was done only in the מקדש. The גמרא then discusses whether the יובל can share ראש השנה's prayer line about creation, and a new משנה opens: a cracked or glued-together שופר is פסול.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the mouth of the שופר was plated with gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה saying the mouthpiece of the ראש השנה שופר in the מקדש was covered with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And its mouth was plated with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה so it can examine it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described the special שופר used on ראש השנה in the מקדש. One detail was gold plating at its mouth. The גמרא picks this detail out because it seems to clash with another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mouth, meaning the end of the שופר you blow into

phrases.english: And its mouth was plated with gold.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, describing the שופר used on ראש השנה in the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראש השנה שופר in the מקדש had gold plating at its mouth.

steps.title: A ברייתא says gold where the mouth goes makes the שופר unfit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a שופר plated with gold at the place where one puts his mouth is פסול, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: if he plated it with gold at the place where he puts his mouth, it is unfit; if not at the place where he puts his mouth, it is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that says gold at the mouthpiece disqualifies a שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gold at the mouth makes a שופר פסול, then the מקדש could not have used a שופר with a gold-plated mouth. Either the משנה or the ברייתא seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The spot where one places his mouth
Unfit, does not work for the מצוה

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: if he plated it with gold
at the place where he puts his mouth, it is unfit,
not at the place where he puts his mouth, it is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's description from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the שופר's mouth was gold-plated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says gold at the mouthpiece makes a שופר פסול, so the מקדש could not have used such a שופר.

steps.title: אביי: the gold in the משנה was not on the mouthpiece itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה also means the gold was not where the mouth is placed, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: when we learned the משנה too, we learned it as being not at the place where the mouth is placed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the משנה more precisely: 'its mouth' means near the mouth, not the exact spot the lips touch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only disqualifies gold on the exact spot where the lips go. אביי says the משנה's gold was a little away from that spot, so it fits the ברייתא's case of כשר. Both sources now agree.
steps.whatToRemember: Gold on the exact spot of the lips makes a שופר פסול. The מקדש's gold was near the mouth but not on that spot.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
when we learned our mishna too,
we learned it as not at the place where the mouth is placed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean gold exactly where the lips go, which the ברייתא says is פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's gold was not on the lip spot, so the שופר was כשר, just as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: two trumpets at the sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next detail of the משנה: two trumpets were blown, one on each side of the שופר blower.
steps.simpleTranslation: And two trumpets at the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the משנה to examine it. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש on ראש השנה, trumpets were blown together with the שופר. This raises a practical problem about hearing the שופר clearly, which the next step brings up.

keyTerms.meaning: Trumpets, metal horns different from a שופר

phrases.english: And two trumpets at the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new detail of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two trumpets were blown alongside the שופר in the מקדש on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Can anyone hear two sounds at once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the שופר could be heard over the trumpets, citing a ברייתא that the human ear cannot take in two sounds at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can two sounds be heard together? Isn't it taught: 'Remember' and 'Keep' were said in one utterance, something the mouth cannot say and the ear cannot hear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if the trumpets and שופר sound together, no one could really hear the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only הקב״ה could say זכור and שמור in one utterance, because people cannot speak or hear two things at once. If so, the trumpets would drown out the שופר, and people would not fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Remember' and 'Keep', the two wordings of the שבת commandment
In one utterance, at the same moment

phrases.english: But can two sounds be heard together?
Isn't it taught: "Remember" and "Keep"
were said in one utterance,
something the mouth cannot say
and the ear cannot hear!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's detail quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that trumpets were blown together with the שופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot hear two sounds at once, so the trumpets would block the שופר and no one would fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: The שופר blast was made longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שופר blast was drawn out longer than the trumpets, so its end could be heard alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why he lengthens the blast with the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שופר was blown longer, so after the trumpets stopped, the שופר could still be heard by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule about two sounds is accepted. The fix is timing: the trumpets stop first, and the last part of the שופר blast is heard clearly on its own.

phrases.english: That is why he lengthens the blast with the shofar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical explanation of how the blowing was done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trumpets would cover the whole שופר blast, so it could not be heard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שופר blast outlasted the trumpets, so its end was heard alone.

steps.title: Does this mean hearing only part of a blast is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out what the answer implies: if hearing only the end of a תקיעה counts, then hearing only the beginning should count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that if he heard the end of a blast without its beginning, he fulfilled his obligation? And so automatically, if he heard the beginning of a blast without its end, he fulfilled his obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what step 6 implies: part of a שופר blast is enough to fulfill the מצוה. This sets up a test of that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, people heard only the end of the שופר blast clearly. If that counts, the same logic says hearing only the beginning counts too. The גמרא now needs to check whether this idea holds up against other sources.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? It introduces an implication being drawn out.

phrases.english: Is this to say that when he heard the end of a blast
without the beginning of the blast, he fulfilled his obligation,
and so automatically, the beginning of a blast
without the end of the blast, he fulfilled his obligation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule out of the answer in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearing only part of a תקיעה, its end or its beginning, is enough to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: A משנה where one long blast counts only once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if someone stretched a תקיעה to the length of two, it counts as only one. If half a blast counts, why not count it as two?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he blew the first one, and drew out the second as long as two, he has only one. Why? Let it count for him as two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea from step 7 against a משנה that seems to say a partial blast does not count on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If half a blast is a full blast, one extra-long תקיעה should count twice: as the end of one set and the start of the next. Yet the משנה says it counts only once. This seems to show that part of a blast does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: He has only one, it counts as one

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he blew the first one,
and drew out the second as long as two,
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the closing תקיעה of a set. He hoped the long blast would also open the next set.

phrases.english: he has only one.
Why? Let it count for him as two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 7 with a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that half a תקיעה counts as a full תקיעה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If half a blast counts, an extra-long blast should count as two, but the משנה says it counts as only one.

steps.title: One blast is never split into two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we do not divide one תקיעה into two, even though hearing part of a blast is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not about hearing part of a blast. It is about splitting one continuous blast into two separate תקיעות, which is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing only the end or only the beginning of a blast does count. But one continuous blast is a single unit and cannot be divided to serve as two תקיעות. So the משנה does not contradict step 7.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא holds that hearing only part of a תקיעה counts, but one long תקיעה can never be split to count as two. The next challenge (step 10) will make the גמרא drop the partial-blast idea in step 11.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer only defends the partial-blast idea against the משנה about one long blast. It is not the last word: after the pit challenge in step 10, the גמרא drops the partial-blast idea in step 11.

phrases.english: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and keeps the inference of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that part of a blast does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Part of a blast does count. The משנה only teaches that one blast cannot be split to serve as two.

steps.title: Blowing into a pit: why doesn't the clear beginning of the blast count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה: if someone blows a שופר into a pit and the listener hears an echo, he has not fulfilled his obligation. If part of a blast is enough, the clear beginning should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone blows into a pit, a cistern, or a large jug. If the listener heard the sound of the שופר, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he heard the sound of an echo, he has not. Why not? He should fulfill his obligation with the beginning of the blast, before the sound got mixed with the echo!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a משנה. It goes against the idea from steps 6–9 that hearing only part of a blast counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6–9 assumed that hearing part of a תקיעה is enough. If so, a person standing outside the pit should fulfill his obligation with the first moment of the blast, before the echo starts. The משנה says he does not, so the idea that part of a blast is enough seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An echo, a blurred sound bouncing back

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who blows into a pit

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַדּוּת אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַפִּיטָס,
phrases.english: or into a cistern, or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the shofar, he has fulfilled his obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שְׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and if he heard the sound of an echo, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
Why? Let him fulfill it with the beginning of the blast,
before the sound becomes mixed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source against the idea, still standing after step 9, that part of a blast counts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from step 6, and the inference from step 7, that hearing part of a תקיעה is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pit case, the first moment of the blast is clear and comes before the echo. If part of a blast counted, the listener would fulfill his obligation. The משנה says he does not.

steps.title: A new answer: two sounds from two different people can be heard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer. The rule that two sounds cannot be heard together applies only to sounds from one source. Two sounds from two different people can be heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: two sounds from one man cannot be heard. Two sounds from two men can be heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the answer from step 6 about a drawn-out blast. It gives a new answer to the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from step 5 is now limited to two sounds coming from one person. The שופר and the trumpets were blown by different people, so the listener can tell them apart. There is no longer any need to say that part of a blast counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the גמרא is dropping its earlier answer
Can be heard, can be told apart

steps.confusionAlert: This does not add to the drawn-out-blast answer. It replaces it. After the pit challenge, the גמרא no longer relies on hearing part of a blast.

phrases.english: Rather:

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְתֵּי קָלֵי מֵחַד גַּבְרָא — לָא מִשְׁתַּמְעִי,
phrases.english: two sounds from one man cannot be heard,
from two men, they can be heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 10 by dropping the step 6 answer and answering step 5 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retreat and replacement: narrows the scope of the ברייתא from step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sounds can never be heard together, so the שופר had to be heard on its own at the end of the blast.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only two sounds from one source cannot be heard. Sounds from two different people, like the שופר and the trumpets, can be heard together.

steps.title: Challenge from reading the תורה: two readers are not allowed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that at the reading of the תורה, two people may not read at once and two may not translate at once. This suggests that even two people's voices cannot be heard together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can sounds from two men really be heard? But a ברייתא teaches: at the reading of the תורה, one person reads and one person translates, as long as there are not two reading and two translating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer from step 11 with a ברייתא about reading the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that voices from two different people can be heard together. The ברייתא forbids two people from reading the תורה at the same time. That suggests listeners cannot follow two voices even from two different people.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches: introduces a source that contradicts
As long as, on condition that

phrases.english: And from two men, can they really be heard?
But it is taught in a baraita:
With the Torah reading, one reads and one translates,
as long as there are not two reading
and two translating!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִתְּרֵי גַבְרֵי מִי מִשְׁתַּמְעִי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new principle stated in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that two sounds from two different people can be heard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two people's voices could be heard together, two people could read the תורה at once. The ברייתא forbids it, which suggests the listener cannot follow both.

steps.title: When something is dear to people, they pay attention and hear it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares שופר to the later part of the same ברייתא: for הלל and מגילה, even ten people may read at once. Because these are dear to the listeners, they pay attention. The same is true of שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like the later part of that ברייתא: with הלל and the מגילה, even ten may read together. We see that since it is dear, a person pays attention. Here too, since the שופר is dear, he pays attention and hears it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to the second half of the same ברייתא, which allows many readers when the reading is dear to the listeners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself makes a distinction. Ordinary reading of the תורה needs one voice, but הלל and מגילה may be read by many people at once because people love them and listen closely. שופר is also dear, so a listener focuses and can pick out its sound from the trumpets.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a source
We see from here, it follows

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer has two parts. Two sounds from two different people can be heard. And when the sound is dear to the listener, like שופר, הלל, or מגילה, he focuses and can pick it out even with other sounds around.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether a sound can be heard depends partly on the listener's attention, not only on the sounds themselves.

phrases.english: This is only similar to the latter clause:
With Hallel and the Megillah, even ten may read.
We see that since it is dear, he pays attention,
here too: since it is dear,
phrases.notes: Here means the שופר blown alongside the trumpets.

phrases.english: he pays attention and hears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 using the second half of the same ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case is compared to a different clause of the same source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule for reading the תורה shows that two voices can never be heard together.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the sound is dear to the listener, he focuses and hears it, as with הלל and מגילה. The שופר is the same.

steps.title: Then why must the שופר blast be long?
steps.stepSummary: If the שופר can be heard together with the trumpets, why does the משנה require the שופר to be blown longer?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why is the שופר blown longer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a detail of the משנה. It says that if the שופר can be heard even while the trumpets are blowing, there should be no need for the שופר to outlast them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that on ראש השנה the שופר blows long and the trumpets blow short. That sounded like it was needed so the שופר could be heard alone at the end. But step 13 just said that people pay attention to a dear מצוה and can hear it even alongside other sounds, so the long blast seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: the ram's horn (or other horn) blown on ראש השנה

phrases.english: But why does he blow long with the shofar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 11 and 13: two sounds from two people can be heard, and a dear sound gets the listener's attention. So it asks what the long שופר blast from step 6 is for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the שופר blows longer than the trumpets
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the listener can already hear the שופר alongside the trumpets, there is no need for the שופר to keep going alone at the end.

steps.title: To show that the day's מצוה is the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The long blast teaches people that the main מצוה of ראש השנה is the שופר, not the trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that people know that the מצוה of the day is with the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the long blast is not needed for hearing. It is there to send a message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra length does not help anyone hear. It marks the שופר as the main instrument, so people do not think the trumpets are the מצוה of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: the special מצוה of this day

steps.whatToRemember: Two sounds from two people can be heard together. The שופר on ראש השנה is blown longer only to show that it is the main מצוה of the day.

phrases.english: To know that the מצוה of the day is with the shofar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the rule: a public sign rather than a hearing requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The long blast was needed so the שופר could be heard alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The long blast shows everyone that the שופר is the main מצוה of the day.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on fast-day שופרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on fast days, the שופרות were curved rams' horns with mouths plated in silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on fast days, the שופרות were the curved horns of rams, and the mouthpiece was plated with silver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said that the ראש השנה שופר had a gold-plated mouth. Now it says the fast-day שופר was plated with silver. That difference is what the גמרא will ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: plated, covered with a layer of metal

phrases.english: And on fast days, with those of rams, curved,
and its mouth is plated with silver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the hearing discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fast-day שופרות are curved rams' horns with silver-plated mouths.

steps.title: Why gold there and silver here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ראש השנה שופר is plated with gold but the fast-day שופר with silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there that it is gold, and what is different here that it is silver?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the different metals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are שופרות used for a public מצוה, yet the משנה gives them different metals. The גמרא wants to know what sets them apart.

phrases.english: What is different there that it is gold,
phrases.notes: "There" means ראש השנה, where the משנה said the mouth was plated with gold.

phrases.english: and what is different here that it is silver?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּזָהָב, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the fast-day שופר uses silver while the ראש השנה שופר uses gold

steps.title: First answer: gathering instruments are silver
steps.stepSummary: Anything used to gather the people together is made of silver, as with the silver trumpets in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: every instrument for gathering people is of silver, as it is written: "Make for yourself two silver trumpets."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. On a fast day the שופר's job is to gather the people, and the Torah made the gathering trumpets out of silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a fast day the community is called together to pray. The Torah commanded משה to make silver trumpets for calling the assembly, so silver fits anything with a gathering purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
a gathering or assembly of people

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כָּל כִּינּוּפְיָא דְּכֶסֶף הוּא,
phrases.english: If you want, say: every gathering is of silver,
phrases.notes: He means that any instrument used to gather people is made of silver.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Make for yourself two trumpets of silver."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כָּל כִּינּוּפְיָא דְּכֶסֶף הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Instruments used to gather people are made of silver, learned from the silver trumpets in the Torah.

steps.title: Second answer: the תורה spares Jewish money
steps.stepSummary: The Torah cares about the money of ישראל, so where it is possible, the cheaper metal, silver, is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the Torah has compassion on the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. Silver costs less than gold, so the fast-day שופר uses silver to save money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer has nothing to do with gathering. It is about cost. That makes it open to a challenge, which comes in the next step: why not save money on ראש השנה too?

keyTerms.meaning: the money of the Jewish people

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The Torah has compassion on the money of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Silver is used to save the people money, since it is cheaper than gold.

steps.title: Then make the ראש השנה שופר silver too
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wants to save money, the ראש השנה שופר should also be plated with silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, let us make it of silver!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. If saving money is the reason, it should apply on ראש השנה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern for the people's money is a general reason. It does not explain why ראש השנה would be different, so the gold plating there seems wasteful.

phrases.english: There too, let us make it of silver!
phrases.notes: "There" again means the שופר of ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the Torah spares Jewish money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If saving money is the reason, it should also apply to the ראש השנה שופר, yet the משנה says that one is plated with gold.

steps.title: Honoring the יום טוב comes first
steps.stepSummary: Even so, honoring the יום טוב is more important than saving money, so the ראש השנה שופר gets gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the honor of the יום טוב is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ראש השנה is a יום טוב, and its honor outweighs the savings. A fast day is not a יום טוב, so silver is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does care about the people's money, but on a יום טוב that concern gives way to honoring the day. On a fast day there is no יום טוב honor to weigh against it, so the cheaper metal is used.
steps.whatToRemember: Fast-day שופרות are silver, either because gathering instruments are silver or to save money. The ראש השנה שופר is gold because honoring the יום טוב comes first.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב עֲדִיף.
phrases.english: Even so, the honor of Yom Tov is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב עֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and saves the second answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranks two values: one concern outweighs the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saving the people's money should apply on every occasion, including ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: On a יום טוב, honoring the day outweighs saving money. Only on a fast day does saving money decide.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל plans to follow the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to put the משנה into practice, using שופר and trumpets together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל thought to act in practice in accordance with our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about someone who wanted to follow the משנה in real life. This sets up רבא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא בר שמואל understood the משנה's setup, with a שופר and trumpets blown together, as a practice for every community. The question is whether that is right.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel
thought to act in practice in accordance with our mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לְמִיעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה's details to asking how far its practice applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא בר שמואל planned to follow the משנה's combination of שופר and trumpets.

steps.title: רבא: this was only in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells him that the משנה's practice was said only about the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: They said this only in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא stops רב פפא בר שמואל's plan. He explains that the משנה describes what was done in the מקדש, not in every place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not reject the משנה. He limits where it applies. Blowing שופר and trumpets together belongs only to the מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with the משנה. He is only saying that its practice was for the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
They said this only in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: לָא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the משנה's practice outside the מקדש. The משנה itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא בר שמואל assumed the משנה describes a practice for everywhere, but it describes only the מקדש.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the combined practice was only in the מקדש. Elsewhere, a place uses either trumpets or a שופר, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא this way: When is this said? In the מקדש. But in the outlying areas, where there are trumpets there is no שופר, and where there is a שופר there are no trumpets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבא. It also explains the rule for places outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that using both instruments together belongs only to the מקדש. Outside it, a fast day uses trumpets alone and ראש השנה uses a שופר alone.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
in what case is this said?

steps.whatToRemember: Only in the מקדש were the שופר and trumpets blown together. Everywhere else, it is one or the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical result: outside the מקדש, the משנה's mixed setup is not followed.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
In what case is this said? In the Temple,
but in the outlying areas,
phrases.notes: This means anywhere outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: a place where there are trumpets, there is no shofar,
a place where there is a shofar, there are no trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's limit from step 23 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's statement that the משנה's practice applies only in the מקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that limits the practice to the מקדש and gives a separate rule for places outside it

steps.title: The Sages limit the custom to the Temple gates and Temple Mount
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון used שופר and trumpets together in their towns, but the חכמים said this was done only at the eastern gates and on הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so did רבי חלפתא set up this practice in ציפורי, and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון in סיכני. When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: this was done only at the eastern gates and on הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It tells of two רבנים who used both instruments outside the מקדש, and the חכמים said that was not right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the clearest part of the proof for רבא. Two great רבנים did exactly what רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to do, and the חכמים rejected it. So the joint שופר-and-trumpet practice belongs only to the מקדש area.

keyTerms.meaning: set up a practice or custom
ציפורי, a town in the Galil
סיכני, a town in the Galil
the eastern gates of the מקדש

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Ḥalafta set up the practice in Tzippori
and Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon in Sikhni,
and when the matter came before the Sages, they said:
they did not act this way

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּשַׁעֲרֵי מִזְרָח וּבְהַר הַבַּיִת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except at the eastern gates and on the Temple Mount alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 24, adding a real-life case and the חכמים's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the combined שופר-and-trumpet practice is only for the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording that the חכמים rejected the practice of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון outside the מקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: Blowing שופר and trumpets together is a מקדש practice only; outside it, a place uses one or the other.

steps.title: The verse behind the Temple-only rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) brings the פסוק 'with trumpets and the sound of a שופר, shout before the King, ה׳' and reads it as: only before ה׳, in the מקדש, are both needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי: What is the source? It is written, 'With trumpets and the sound of a שופר, shout before the King, ה׳.' Only before the King, ה׳, do we need trumpets and שופר together, but in general, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for the rule that only the מקדש uses both instruments together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'before the King, ה׳' are read as pointing to the מקדש, where we stand before ה׳. So the pairing of trumpets and שופר is tied to that place, and anywhere else it is not needed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
What is the verse? As it is written:
"With trumpets and the sound of a shofar
shout before the King, the Lord,"
it is before the King, the Lord, that we need
phrases.notes: 'Before ה׳' is understood as the מקדש.

phrases.english: trumpets and the sound of a shofar,
but in general, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proved the rule, this step supplies the פסוק that the rule comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trumpets and שופר together are needed only 'before ה׳', in the מקדש; elsewhere they are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the topic of trumpets and שופר by grounding רבא's limit in a פסוק, not just in practice.

steps.title: Our ראש השנה prayer follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the יובל matches ראש השנה for תקיעות and ברכות. רב שמואל בר יצחק says our prayer 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' follows רבי אליעזר, who holds the world was created in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the יובל is like ראש השנה for the תקיעות and the ברכות. רב שמואל בר יצחק said: whose opinion do we follow when we pray today, 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day'? רבי אליעזר's, who said the world was created in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the יובל. רב שמואל בר יצחק explains which opinion our ראש השנה prayer is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling ראש השנה 'the beginning of Your works' only makes sense if creation began in תשרי. That is רבי אליעזר's view, so our prayer follows him. This sets up the question in the next step about whether the יובל can share this line.

keyTerms.meaning: the 50th year; its יום כיפור has special שופר blowing
the special ברכות added to the עמידה

phrases.english: The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה; it means יום כיפור of the יובל year.

phrases.english: for the blowing and for the blessings, etc.
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
According to whom do we pray today
"This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day"?
According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: The world was created in Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא moves from trumpets to the משנה's line comparing the יובל with ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראש השנה prayer 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' follows רבי אליעזר, that the world was created in תשרי.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Same as ראש השנה' in the משנה is about יום כיפור of the יובל year, not ראש השנה of that year.

steps.title: How can the יובל share a line that fits only ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא objects: the משנה says the יובל has the same ברכות as ראש השנה, but 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' is true only on ראש השנה, not on the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא objected: the משנה says the יובל is like ראש השנה for the תקיעות and the ברכות. But there is the line 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day,' which is said on ראש השנה and not on the יובל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא challenges the משנה using the prayer line just mentioned. He shows that the ברכות cannot be fully the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 showed this line is about creation, which fits ראש השנה only. יום כיפור of the יובל is not the day creation began. So if the משנה says the ברכות are identical, there seems to be a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: it is there / it is not there

phrases.english: Rav Eina raised an objection:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
for the blowing and for the blessings,
but there is "This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day,"
which is there on Rosh HaShana,
but is not there on the Jubilee!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the prayer line from step 27 to challenge the משנה's claim that the ברכות are the same.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the יובל and ראש השנה share the same ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One line of the ראש השנה ברכות speaks of creation, which does not fit יום כיפור of the יובל, so the ברכות cannot be fully identical.

steps.title: The משנה means the rest of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'same' refers to the rest of the ברכות; the line about creation is left out on the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches that they are the same, it is talking about the rest of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב עינא's objection by narrowing what the משנה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה never meant every single word is the same. The main ברכות match, but the creation line 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' is said only on ראש השנה. So there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it is about the rest.
phrases.notes: He means the rest of the ברכות; the creation line is simply not said on the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עינא's objection from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say every word of the ברכות is identical on the יובל and ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the rest of the ברכות are identical; the creation line is said only on ראש השנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The יובל shares ראש השנה's ברכות, except for 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך', which belongs only to ראש השנה.

steps.title: A second version: the משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי reports a different version of רב שמואל בר יצחק's teaching. Here, רב שמואל בר יצחק says the משנה equating the יובל with ראש השנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, taught it like this. רב שמואל בר יצחק said: the משנה says the יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and the ברכות. Whose opinion is that? It cannot be רבי אליעזר. He holds the world was created in תשרי, so we say 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day.' That line belongs on ראש השנה but not on the יובל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the earlier teaching. In this version, רב שמואל בר יצחק himself raises the problem and concludes that the משנה is not like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב שמואל בר יצחק said our prayer follows רבי אליעזר, and רב עינא raised the objection. Here the same problem is used differently. According to רבי אליעזר, the ברכות of the יובל cannot be fully 'the same' as ראש השנה, so רב שמואל בר יצחק says the משנה must follow a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way (introduces a second version of a teaching)
Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
A remembrance of the first day (of creation), a line in the ראש השנה prayer

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion from steps 27–29, told in a different version. Here the problem with 'זה היום' leads רב שמואל בר יצחק to say the משנה is not like רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi,
taught it this way:
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
That which we learned in the mishnah:
the Yovel is the same as Rosh HaShanah
for the blowing and for the blessings,
like whom is it? Not like Rabbi Eliezer,
for if it were Rabbi Eliezer,
since he said
the world was created in Tishrei,
then there is the line
"This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day,"
which fits on Rosh HaShanah
but does not fit on the Yovel!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 27–29 in a different version. Here רב שמואל בר יצחק himself uses the 'זה היום' problem to say the משנה is not like רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה equating the ברכות of the יובל with those of ראש השנה does not follow רבי אליעזר, because by his view 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' applies only on ראש השנה.

steps.title: The משנה means the rest of the ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר. The משנה's 'same' refers to the rest of the ברכות, not the creation line.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה says 'the same,' it is talking about the rest of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב שמואל בר יצחק's conclusion. The משנה can follow רבי אליעזר after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that one line, 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך', fits ראש השנה but not the יובל. The גמרא answers that 'the same' was never meant to include every word. It refers to the rest of the ברכות, and that one line is dropped on the יובל. This is the same answer as step 29, but here it knocks down the claim that the משנה is not like רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: When it teaches (this): what the source is really talking about
On the rest, the other parts

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the conclusion is the same: the יובל's ברכות match ראש השנה except for the line about creation, so the משנה can fit רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it refers to the rest.
phrases.notes: The rest of the ברכות. Only the line about creation is left out on the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 30's conclusion by narrowing the משנה's word 'same' to the rest of the ברכות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed that 'the same' must include every single line of the ברכות, including the creation line.

steps.title: A cracked or glued-together שופר is פסול
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A שופר that cracked and was glued back together is פסול. A שופר made by gluing together broken pieces of שופרות is also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A שופר that cracked and was glued together is unfit. If someone glued together broken pieces of שופרות, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: which damaged or repaired שופרות may be used. It gives two cases, and both are פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is one שופר that cracked and was glued back together. The second case is a 'שופר' built from glued-together pieces of different שופרות. In both cases the repaired שופר is ruled פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Unfit, cannot be used for the מצוה

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A shofar that cracked and he glued it together
is unfit.
If he glued together broken pieces of shofars,
it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the יובל discussion and opens a new משנה about damaged and repaired שופרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cracked שופר that was glued, or a שופר made from glued broken pieces, is פסול.
